Dense labeling prevented tracing complete individual neurons. The supplementary estimate of 20-80 sampled cells per mouse is not an identified neuron census. The study total of 32079 spines in 209 mice does not make spines independent animals or mean that every spine was followed for 120 days.

Formation and elimination are interval-specific percentages relative to the initial spine count. New-spine survival uses the newly appearing subset instead. These denominators cannot be exchanged or converted into universal growth rates, absolute density or graph weights.

Main scientific text, Methods Summary and Figures 1-4 are reviewed. All text of the 12-page publisher supplement, Figures S1-S5 and Table S1 are reviewed, including visual inspection. The separate full Methods file and movie were not obtained or read; precise task procedures, sex, allocation, blinding and exclusions remain unverified.

Dense labeling prevented tracing complete individual neurons. The supplementary estimate of 20-80 sampled cells per mouse is not an identified neuron census. The study total of 32079 spines in 209 mice does not make spines independent animals or mean that every spine was followed for 120 days.

Formation and elimination are interval-specific percentages relative to the initial spine count. New-spine survival uses the newly appearing subset instead. These denominators cannot be exchanged or converted into universal growth rates, absolute density or graph weights.

General controls were littermates with the same food restriction and similar handling, without shaping or training. Learning, task exposure and reward are not individually isolated. Animal-level image stacks, cohort assignments and analysis code were not obtained; published tests were not independently reproduced.

Imaging occurred within one hour after the session, but the baseline was from the previous day; this interval does not timestamp each spine birth within an hour.

Behavioral curves, spine-turnover cohorts and follow-up cohorts have different animal counts. The survival design uses two classification images and a third follow-up at a selected interval; it is not one fully sampled trajectory through every plotted timepoint.

Figure 2c normalizes total spine number to the initial image. Both control and trained trajectories lie below their initial value by day 16. Convergence toward control levels is distinct from the abstract wording about return to the original level; no exact count setpoint or one-for-one replacement is demonstrated.

Spine morphology does not directly measure synaptic currents, presynaptic partner identity or memory content. The study does not selectively remove the retained spines to test memory necessity or uniquely assign different memories to disjoint synaptic sets.

Motor mapping was terminal in fourteen mice: five imaging regions lay within the forelimb map, six on its border and three outside but within 300 micrometers. The map was not followed longitudinally, and distance from its border does not identify a complete circuit or a construction geometry.

Named nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The long-duration activity controls had marked attrition: only two mice still reached more than twenty times daily at day eight and one at day sixteen. They do not support a well-powered universal exclusion of motor activity.
